observed_item: Gothic/medieval-fantasy mood: flowing capes (Gabriela Hearst), femme-fatale corsets with diffused lace (McQueen), botanical embroidery + Art Deco jewelry on eveningwear (Givenchy)
notes: Season-framing piece by Vogue Korea: F/W 2026 defined by 'fantasy vs reality'. Signals escapism-leaning styling for party/occasion wear relevant to Korean 20s-30s evening contexts.

observed_item: 1920s Art Deco eveningwear: beaded tunic dresses (Lanvin, Prada), beaded embroidery for red-carpet/party; tulle cited as the material that opened the season; article explicitly frames this as a departure from several seasons of 'quiet luxury' minimalism
notes: Direct claim that ornament/beading replaces minimalism this season — a key directional signal for occasion wear bought by Korean 20s-early30s consumers.

observed_item: 12 F/W menswear trends incl.: Preppy 3.0 (corduroy duffle coats with toggle buttons, sporty mix, Yohji Yamamoto/Sacai), Matrix-style long black coats, ski sweaters, 1960s clean-silhouette tailoring (Thom Browne, Junya Watanabe), boiler suits (utility), white suits/pants as luxury code
silhouette: long overcoat; 1960s slim-clean tailoring; boiler suit
notes: Vogue Korea's own 12-trend menswear map for the exact season target. Duffle coats, Matrix long coats and preppy styling map directly to Korean menswear retail.

observed_item: Texture push in menswear: jacquard and cut velvet across men's collections (Jonathan Anderson/Paul Poiret inspiration); small fur trims at neck and cuffs as 'texture + warmth + quiet luxury'; heavy black leather with sharp silhouettes (punk/Richard Hell/CBGB)
material: jacquard, cut velvet, fur trim, black leather
notes: Men's fabrics explicitly borrow 'women's luxury materials' — a concrete material trend for Korean menswear 20s-30s (velvet/leather outer, fur-trim collars).

observed_item: Silk scarf 'foulard' described as crossing gender lines: scarf dressing (tied at neck or worn as full-pattern covering) appears across collections; also lumberjack/outdoor codes — buffalo check, camouflage, military green — plus a pink wave in menswear following the J.Crew pink-sweater debate (Nov 2025)
notes: Explicit genderless styling claim (scarves) + outdoor-lumberjack palette + pink as a men's color. Scarf dressing is an accessible entry point for Korean male consumers.

observed_item: 'Slender Man' silhouette shift: after years of oversize, Prada (Miuccia Prada/Raf Simons), Dior Men (Jonathan Anderson) and Gucci (Demna) all cut volume out — skinny pants matched with same-material suit jacket with bare waist exposed; cropped-at-waist wool bar jackets; sparkly party tops with rock'n'roll jeans; body-skimming shirts showing muscle line; Prada S/S 2027 continues fitted jacket + slim pants
silhouette: slim/skinny trousers; cropped boxy-bar jacket; fitted jacket
notes: Strongest single directional claim for Korean menswear: editorial explicitly says oversize is ending and slim is returning — ahead of the F/W buying window for 20s-30s men.

observed_item: F/W 2026 trend themes: couture-level handcraft in RTW (stitch embroidery, crochet, sequins, lace, swinging fringe — Rabanne/Dior/Chanel/Etro/Miu Miu); H-line knee-length pencil midi skirts in leather/glitter/wool styled with cinched waist + heels (Victoria Beckham, Isabel Marant, Marni, Mugler); black jackets with bold statement buttons buttoned to the top (Dior, LV)
silhouette: H-line pencil midi skirt; single/double-breasted jacket, buttoned-to-neck
material: leather, glitter, wool, sequins, crochet, fringe
notes: Concrete tops-bottoms pairing guidance: black button-up jacket × pencil midi skirt × heels = 'city chic' — directly replicable styling for Korean office-to-evening wear.

observed_item: New Romanticism: white-to-soft-pastel palette, sheer fabrics and delicate lace in bold voluminous shapes; 17th-century rococo corset details, petticoats, bow trims (McQueen, Chloé, Zimmermann, Alberta Ferretti, Simone Rocha). Also 1980s punk return: vintage slogan tees, destroyed pants, big-shoulder jackets, black leather accessories, studs, tartan check
silhouette: voluminous; strong-shouldered jacket; destroyed slim pants
notes: Two-opposite-poles season (romantic sheer/volume vs punk leather/studs) — both youth-culture-friendly codes for Korean 20s audience.

observed_item: Olive named THE fall color: cropped olive jackets to floor-length olive trench coats (Zimmermann belted jacket, Valentino long lean coat); olive suede jacket styled with denim or cream pants; olive leather coat with brown accessories; olive silk dress (Tory Burch NYFW); olive lace mini and slip dress (Saint Laurent); olive suede shoulder bags/totes (Bottega, Chanel, Ferragamo Hug East-West); olive pumps (LV), olive suede shoes (Mugler)
color: olive (with brown, caramel, burgundy, cream, khaki pairings)
silhouette: cropped jacket; long trench; slip dress; mini dress
notes: Full head-to-toe olive color story with explicit styling rules (olive suede × denim/cream pants; texture-mixing over color-matching). Highly actionable for Korean fall wardrobes.

observed_item: '2026 F/W Runway Notes' editor round-up: vintage slip dresses return with faded pastels/browns, lace trims, beading, irregular hems — layered OVER capri pants or lace skirts and styled with sneakers; opera gloves worn with knit dresses and minimal tops+pants as daily wear; thigh-high boots restyled with voluminous knits, denim pants and modest tailoring instead of miniskirts
notes: Concrete layering formulas (slip dress × capri pants × sneakers) that translate directly to Korean 20s street styling — vintage-romantic but worn casually.

observed_item: 'Go Big' fur: oversized faux-fur/alternative-material fur coats dominate (Valentino, Tom Ford, Gucci, Balenciaga, Chanel, Bottega); belt-waisted cocoon fur coat (Saint Laurent) called editor's pick; multicolor fur coats/fur vests/fur bags (Chanel, Diesel, Fendi); 'shrinkmaxxing' counterpoint — contracted silhouettes in gray coats, e.g. Miu Miu's narrow rounded shoulders and short sleeves exposing wrists
silhouette: oversized fur coat; belted cocoon coat; shrunken narrow-shoulder coat
notes: Volume fur is the season's outer statement, with a shrunken-silhouette counter-trend — two clear outerwear directions for the Korean winter coat market.

observed_item: 'Wrap it up': scarves/mufflers promoted to focal styling item — exaggerated mufflers changing coat proportions (Celine/Michael Rider), air-inflated tube scarves maximizing neck volume (Loewe), color-block mufflers worn casually (Prada); 'Purple Rain': purple leather trench coat + bag (Celine), purple puff-sleeve blouse with two-tone purple pants (Chloé); animal print surge — leopard coats (Celine, Givenchy), calf-hair coat + animal-print shoes (Marni), tiger-print vest/coat (Fendi); pearls extending into menswear in the 'gender-cross era'; sporty wraparound sunglasses worn with dresses/tailoring; sculptural oversized hats (Jacquemus, Loewe, Givenchy)
notes: Dense editor-verified keyword set: scarf-as-styling and purple are the two most actionable items here; pearls-into-menswear is a direct gender-expression observation.

observed_item: 'Troublesome Student' preppy: ruffle blouses + tiered check skirts + oversize blazers (Chloé bohemian preppy), ankle-length long coats + avant-garde jacket + shirt + tie + thigh-high boots (Dries Van Noten) — preppy recast as a rebellious, just-ran-out-of-class attitude rather than Ivy neatness; also 'Simple Life': clean cotton poplin/linen shirts and skirts (Prada, Jil Sander, The Row, Gucci); 'Code Red': vivid red across elegant dresses (Chanel, Alaïa), sheer red dresses (Chloé, Bluemarine), sharp red leather (Balenciaga)
silhouette: oversize blazer; tiered skirt; long ankle coat
notes: Korean editors explicitly redefine preppy as 'rebellious student' — matches the Vogue Korea menswear 'Preppy 3.0' claim from another publisher, strengthening the preppy signal.

observed_item: 'Classic Woman Returns': skirt suits in gold-sequin tweed (Chanel), 1950s cinched-waist suits (Lanvin), pencil skirt + pocket-detail tailored jacket (Tom Ford); 'The New Match': white × beige tonal layering worn head-to-toe with matching bags/shoes (Celine, Bottega, Toteme, Miu Miu, Tory Burch); 'Powerful Checks': big tartan/plaid worn as full set-ups, not accent pieces (LV, Chloé, Loewe, Acne Studios); big shoulder bags incl. laptop-size; oversized 3D flower brooch/corsage in feather/ribbon/leather/crystal; train details on satin tops and tuxedos; T-strap heels with midi skirts; sculptural ear cuffs (Saint Laurent); slimmed Celine tailoring with off-angle flare pants + bucket/derby hats + stiff scarves
silhouette: skirt suit; pencil skirt; full check set-up; flare pants
notes: Most styling-dense single page found: tonal white-beige layering and check set-ups are concrete, copyable Korean-fall looks; skirt-suit revival crosses office/occasion contexts.

observed_item: All-black restyled via texture and silhouette instead of color: Demna's Gucci — fitted black jacket + slim pants + black bag + pointed shoes (90s sensual code); black top × wide Bermuda pants + long silver necklace (office-to-weekend); Chanel (Matthieu Blazy) — black knit jacket + pencil skirt + gold buttons lifted by burgundy bag/shoes; D&G — waist-emphasized black jacket × full midi skirt; black turtleneck sleeveless + slim pants with ankle exposed + strappy sandals
silhouette: fitted jacket + slim pants; wide Bermuda pants; pencil skirt; full midi skirt
notes: Concrete top×bottom all-black formulas (incl. Bermuda pants pairing) framed around Korean office-to-weekend use — directly reusable for a Korean 20s-30s wardrobe.

observed_item: 7 F/W runway keywords: (1) flower motifs on dresses/jackets/accessories (Chanel, Dior, Givenchy, Erdem); (2) bold colorful checks + mixed-scale check-clashing (Celine, Chloé, Chanel, Dries Van Noten, Acne); (3) fluffy fur outerwear from twee to monumental oversized (Chanel, Bottega, Saint Laurent, Gucci, Burberry); (4) gender-boundary-erasing office suiting — widened shoulders, precisely cut jackets, pants suits framed as the new 'career woman uniform' (Dior, D&G, Givenchy, Saint Laurent); (5) minimal body-con dresses (Alaïa, Gucci) with Prada/Miu Miu relaxed alternative; (6) leather turned soft/fluid — body-following leather looks (Gucci, Hermès), clean glossy leather (Prada, Ferragamo); (7) reinforced black — power shoulders, structural tailoring, mixed-material black-on-black (Alaïa, Balenciaga)
silhouette: power shoulder; body-con dress; relaxed shirting
notes: Independent Korean confirmation of fur/black/check/leather trends and an explicit genderless-suiting claim; covers both occasion and office wear for the target demo.

observed_item: Fall 2026 color list: red everywhere incl. bright turtlenecks (Celine, Lii) and tonal red-on-pink layering (Celine); royal purple across RTW and accessories (Celine, Loewe, Mugler, Tory Burch, Balenciaga); electric/cobalt blue incl. Klein-blue textured look (Bottega) and cobalt with navy (Givenchy) or gray (Jil Sander); butter yellow (Dior, Kallmeyer, Tod's, Chloé); juicy peach/melon in knits and corduroys (Tory Burch), embellished dresses (Chanel), minis (Miu Miu); turquoise entering fall; burgundy as cold-weather classic
color: red, royal purple, cobalt blue, butter yellow, peach/melon, turquoise, burgundy
notes: International color map aligning with Korean editors (purple, red) plus extensions (cobalt, peach, butter yellow) usable to widen a Korean fall palette.

observed_item: 6 key F/W 2026 trends: 'Power of Styling' — re-pairing existing staples like cardigans and workwear jackets, layered basics, unexpected accessories (Prada-led); 'Updated Lady' — softened power suiting with gently sloping waists and sculpted jackets (Chanel, Givenchy, Balenciaga, Celine); 'Go Figure' — body-conscious: second-skin dresses (Alaïa), sheer layers (Khaite), lingerie slips (Valentino), styled as knit bustier + slim trouser (Jil Sander) or sheer mini + slip + over-the-knee boots (Cos); 1920s Art Deco touches (Khaite, Dries Van Noten, Loro Piana); reworked proportions (Ashlyn, Christopher John Rogers)
silhouette: sculpted jacket; sloping waist; second-skin dress; slim trouser
notes: International anchor source: 'staging over newness' layering and softened-tailoring narrative matches Korean coverage; confirms sheer/slip + OTK boot formulas seen in Bazaar Korea.

observed_item: Article claims 1970s-80s leopard full coats/jackets are a 2026 F/W trend ('올가을은 애니멀 프린트 참지 말고 입어도 됩니다') — title/summary only, page not fully fetched
notes: SECONDARY claim from search-level summary, corroborating Bazaar Korea's animal-print runway note. Treat as article's claim, not independently verified page content.
